questions.q: A loss curve logged at the batch level looks jagged even though training is proceeding normally. What does this usually indicate?
options: The model is diverging and training should be stopped
Each batch's loss is a noisy sample of the true loss; the real signal is in the trend over many batches or epochs, not any single point
There is a bug in the loss function
The learning rate is far too high
questions.explain: Per-batch loss naturally fluctuates because each batch is a different sample. This is expected noise, not a problem — judge training by the overall trend (often via epoch averages or a moving average), not individual jagged points.

questions.q: What pattern in a loss curve is the classic signature of overfitting?
options: Both training and validation loss plateau at the same value
Training loss keeps falling while validation loss flattens out or starts rising, widening the gap between them
Training loss spikes briefly then recovers
Both losses diverge toward infinity together
questions.explain: A widening train/validation gap — training loss still improving while validation loss stalls or worsens — means the model is increasingly fitting training-specific noise rather than generalizing.

questions.q: Both training and validation loss flatten out much earlier than expected, well before convergence should occur. What are the two most likely explanations?
options: Data leakage and an incorrect loss function
A learning rate that is too low, or the model has run out of capacity for the data as given
GPU memory exhaustion and a corrupted dataset
Too many validation samples
questions.explain: A premature plateau commonly points to either a learning rate too small to keep making progress, or a model that has genuinely reached the limit of what it can represent given its current architecture.

questions.q: What does outright loss divergence — loss climbing and climbing, eventually toward inf or nan — usually signal?
options: The dataset is too small
The learning rate is too high outright, or gradients are exploding
The validation set is misconfigured
This is actually a sign of healthy, fast convergence
questions.explain: Sustained divergence toward inf/nan is a strong signal that the optimizer is taking steps too large to be stable — most commonly from too high a learning rate or exploding gradients.

questions.q: Why is it a good habit to plot both training and validation loss on the same chart rather than just training loss alone?
options: Validation loss is always lower and makes the chart look better
Looking at training loss alone can hide overfitting, since training loss can keep improving even as the model generalizes worse
Matplotlib requires at least two series per plot
Validation loss is computed faster and should replace training loss entirely
questions.explain: Training loss alone will often keep dropping even as the model overfits. Only by comparing it against validation loss can you catch the widening gap that signals the model is memorizing rather than generalizing.
